results.title: NVIDIA H100 SXM5 GPU Use Cases on Massed Compute - Massed Compute
results.author: Gabe Mills
highlights:
## NVIDIA H100 SXM5 Use Cases, Pricing, and When to Launch 1x or 8x

Gabe Mills, Massed Compute September 2026

Serve a 70B-class model, hold a long context, or train across GPUs that share an NVLink fabric. Massed Compute launches NVIDIA H100 SXM5 for that work as one 80 GB module or as an eight-GPU box. You pick `gpu_1x_H100_SXM5` or `gpu_8x_H100_SXM5` on Deploy. The cards are already in the machine.

A 1x instance is $2.89 an hour as of 16 September 2026. Confirm live 1x and 8x rates on GPU pricing before you launch.

Stay on 1x when weights plus KV still fit 80 GB. Take 8x when you need 16-bit 70B, a cache that spills one card, or tensor parallel across NVLink.

If the model already fits 32 GB or 48 GB, start on that card. This page is the 80 GB Hopper SXM5 product.

...

This article is H100 SXM5. Hopper SXM, 80 GB HBM3, NVLink on the 8x box. SKUs `gpu_1x_H100_SXM5` and `gpu_8x_H100_SXM5`. The live catalog has no 2x or 4x SXM5.

H100 PCIe 80 GB is a different board. Live 1x is `gpu_1x_h100`. 2x is `gpu_2x_h100`. 4x is `gpu_4x_h100`. Guides that say “launch a 2x H100” mean this family.

...

## 1x and 8x shapes

On demand has no contract and no minimum. You pay for the hours you use. Confirm live pricing before you launch.

`gpu_1x_H100_SXM5` is one 80 GB module, 14 vCPU, 122 GiB RAM, and 350 GB disk. `gpu_8x_H100_SXM5` is eight modules (640 GB combined), 126 vCPU, 976 GiB RAM, and 2,800 GB disk.

You are renting one eight-GPU NVLink box, not eight separate 1x VMs. Memory, RAM, and disk scale with the eight modules. vCPU does not land on a clean 8×. You get 126, not 112. A request that already fits 80 GB does not get eight times faster on eight cards.

Use 8x when the model, the KV cache, or the training shard plan does not fit one 80 GB GPU. Stay on 1x when a single module already holds the work.

...

We launched a Massed Compute 1x H100 SXM5 on 10 September 2026. Ubuntu Server 24.04 with NVIDIA drivers. SKU `gpu_1x_H100_SXM5`. Hardware only. No model was served, so this page does not invent 1x tok/s.

| --- | --- | --- |
| GPU | 1x H100 SXM5 (80GB) | `nvidia-smi` name NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3. `lspci` GH100 [H100 SXM5 80GB] |
| GPU memory | 80 GB | 81559 MiB (79.6 GiB). Idle free 81079 MiB |
| Driver | Ubuntu 24.04 with drivers | 580.126.16. CUDA 13.0 in `nvidia-smi`. Compute capability 9.0 |
| vCPU | 14 | `nproc` 14. Xeon Platinum 8592V, CPU list 0-13 |
| System RAM | 122 GiB | about 120 GiB usable in MemTotal |
| Disk | 350 GB | 344G formatted on `/` (320G free on this fresh image) |
| NVLink | 8x fabric | 1x topology is a single GPU. NVLink links inactive. No NV# peer |

...

### What does 1x H100 SXM5 cost per hour?

$2.89 on demand with no contract, current as of 16 September 2026. Confirm live 1x and 8x rates on GPU pricing before you launch.

### What GPU type do I pick on Deploy?

H100 SXM5 (80GB). Then pick quantity ×1 or ×8. That maps to `gpu_1x_H100_SXM5` and `gpu_8x_H100_SXM5`.

...

### Is 8x eight times the 1x price?

No. The 8x SKU includes more RAM, more disk, and NVLink. You rent one eight-GPU box. Check live 1x and 8x rates on GPU pricing.

...

## Launch H100 SXM5

Check live GPU pricing, then launch `gpu_1x_H100_SXM5` or `gpu_8x_H100_SXM5`.

results.author: GPUIndexes Research
highlights:
GPUINDEXES RESEARCH Sep 13, 2026

## The first observation

At 04:35 UTC on Sep 13, 2026, our first H100 SXM 80 GB snapshot contained 9 eligible single-GPU offer configurations from 6 providers. The provider-floor median was $3.08 per GPU-hour, with qualifying provider floors ranging from $2.79 to $4.29.

| Provider | Lowest eligible quote | Region |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lyceum | $2.7900 / GPU-hour | Europe |
| Massed Compute | $2.8900 / GPU-hour | us-central-12 |
| Ori | $2.9000 / GPU-hour | dallas-2 |
| VERDA | $3.2500 / GPU-hour | FIN-HEL |
| RunPod | $3.4900 / GPU-hour | global |
| Lambda Labs | $4.2900 / GPU-hour | us-south-3 |

## Why the basket matters

An H100 PCIe offer is not an H100 SXM offer. A price per GPU inside an eight-GPU instance does not mean that a single GPU can be rented at that price. The initial series fixes the model, memory, instance size and pricing lane before calculating a reference.

## A reference, not a transaction

The lowest provider quote is an observed floor. The median across providers describes the middle of those floors, with equal provider weight. It does not estimate the price of a typical completed transaction, the amount of supply, or every user’s total bill.

## From an observation to a time series

This first point establishes a record. Future changes require future observations. We have not backfilled this series with older catalog averages that mix unavailable stock, spot offers and different configurations.

The complete methodology describes those decisions and the data API provides access to the daily record. This note remains tied to the first saved observation even as the live dashboard changes.

results.title: NVIDIA H100 Price: Buying vs Renting per Hour
results.author: Faiz Ahmed
highlights:
The honest answer is $25,000 to $36,000 for one H100 card, and NVIDIA does not publish a list price. The low end is the street price Tom's Hardware reported for the PCIe version in August 2023, and the high end is what CNBC said some retailers had asked before April 2023, without naming the version. A distributor still listed it at $35,315.93 on 2026-09-28, and eBay listings went past $40,000 in 2023. Renting the same GPU on QuantaCloud costs $2.59/GPU-hr. At the $2.59 per GPU-hour it cost on 2026-09-27, a card at $25,000 to $35,316 equals 9,653 to 13,635 hours of rental, which is 13 to 19 months of round-the-clock use (our calculation, below). The SXM H100 has no card price I can quote: it ships on 4- and 8-GPU HGX boards inside complete servers.

...

An H100 PCIe rents for $2.59/GPU-hr on QuantaCloud, billed by the hour. These are the live configurations:

| GPUs | vCPU | RAM | Disk | Region | Per hour | Per GPU-hour | Launch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1x H100 PCIe | 20 | 128 GB | 1,250 GB | us-midwest-2 | $2.59 | $2.59 | Launch |
| 2x H100 PCIe | 40 | 256 GB | 2,500 GB | us-midwest-2 | $5.18 | $2.59 | Launch |

Prices checked 14 Nov 2026, 13:25 UTC

The hourly price covers a whole VM, not only the GPU. On 2026-09-27 the single-GPU H100 VM came with 20 vCPU, 128 GB of RAM and 1,250 GB of disk in us-midwest-2, running Ubuntu 22.04 with the NVIDIA driver and Docker. Billing runs from a prepaid balance with a $5 minimum deposit. The first hour is charged at launch, each further hour is charged when the previous one is used up, and the unused seconds of the current hour are refunded when you stop. There are no egress or ingress charges. Stopping terminates the VM and deletes its disk, so copy your results off first. The pricing page and the billing docs have the full rules, and the H100 page covers the specs and what fits in 80 GB. The GPU cost calculator applies those rules to your own hours at the live price. SXM H100 servers are not on demand: they are the reserved builds described above.

results.title: GPU pricing is increasing across the board, but the severity of those increases varies greatly across providers.
highlights:
# GPU pricing is increasing across the board, but the severity of those increases varies greatly across providers. · 2026-09-22T00:00:00+00:00

GPU pricing is increasing across the board, but the severity of those increases varies greatly across providers.

Take H100 pricing as an example.

In 2026, providers in our network have raised their H100 rates by an average of 31.6%.

However, between these providers, their individual H100 pricing has increased as much as 47.5%, and as little as 13.6%.

Movement in GPU pricing as a whole only tells part of the story.

There is still significant price variance between operators, even those with near identical architectures.

results.title: Cheapest H100 Rental: Prices by Provider and the Catch · Aliteq
results.author: Aliteq Team
highlights:
The cheapest H100 you could rent on Nov 3, 2026 was $1.79 an hour, on-demand, on Vast.ai's marketplace (median $2.40 across 6 offers, our 12:20 UTC read). The cheapest managed H100s were Hyperstack at $2.50 (listed simply as "H100") and Runpod Secure Cloud at $2.89 for an H100 PCIe. The catch: Vast's floor is one host out of a handful and can be gone in an hour, the even cheaper interruptible H100s can be paused or taken back mid-job, and on both Vast and Runpod the storage keeps billing after you stop the instance. Lambda, Nebius and CoreWeave listed $3.29 to $6.16 for the same chip that day. For the price right now, see our live cloud-GPU compare page.

## The short answer (read Nov 3, 2026)

The cheapest on-demand H100 on Nov 3, 2026 was $1.79 an hour on Vast.ai's marketplace (median $2.40 across 6 H100 SXM offers). Managed alternatives were Hyperstack at $2.50 and Runpod Secure Cloud at $2.89 (H100 PCIe) or $3.99 (H100 SXM). Interruptible H100s went lower: Vast from $0.89 and Nebius preemptible from $0.79, but Vast's docs say an interruptible instance may be paused if outbid. Enterprise clouds listed the same chip at $3.29 (Lambda PCIe) to $6.16 (CoreWeave, per GPU on an 8-GPU node). Storage is billed while an instance is stopped on Vast and Runpod, so delete what you don't need.

...

Our Nov 12 read (17:20 UTC) of the same feeds: the cheapest on-demand H100 was an H100 PCIe at $1.95 an hour on Lium (one offer), then Vast.ai's H100 SXM from $2.20 (median $2.20 across 13 offers; Vast's H100 PCIe from $2.54, H100 NVL from $2.34) and Lium's H100 SXM at $2.50. Runpod Secure Cloud was unchanged at $2.89 (PCIe), $3.19 (NVL) and $3.99 (SXM). Interruptible H100s started at $1.20 on Lium and $0.27 on Vast, where the median interruptible SXM bid was $2.13.
